title: Lesson 55 - Cross-Component Performance Optimization: OmniScript Load Time, IP Execution, Data Mapper Queries
description: Recommend strategies for performance optimization strategies across all components (Omniscript load time, IP execution, Data Mapper queries) to ensure scalable and efficient solutions.

questions.question: An OmniScript feels slow on the first step even though the server is fast. Which change is most likely to help?
options: Add more Data Raptors to the first step so all data is ready
Defer data loading to the step that needs it and load only displayed fields
Increase the row limit on every Data Raptor
Move all logic into a single Integration Procedure
questions.explanation: Deferring data loading and loading only displayed fields reduces the work done on the first render, which is what the user perceives as slow. Adding more Data Raptors makes the first step slower. Increasing row limits returns more data and worsens the problem. Moving all logic into one IP does not address the load-time queries and may add a round trip.

questions.question: An Integration Procedure calls the same external system three times in a loop to gather data. What is the best optimization?
options: Keep the loop but add a longer timeout
Batch the calls into a single request and return only needed fields
Move the loop into the OmniScript
Cache the external system's entire database in Salesforce
questions.explanation: Batching the calls into a single request reduces round trips, and returning only needed fields keeps the payload small, which directly cuts latency. A longer timeout does not reduce the number of calls. Moving the loop into the OmniScript just relocates the problem to the browser. Caching the entire external database is not feasible or appropriate.

questions.question: A Data Raptor that filters on a non-indexed field is slow and returns thousands of rows. What is the correct fix?
options: Remove the filter so the query returns everything
Filter on an indexed field and add a row limit where the business allows
Run the query inside a loop to split the work
Convert the Data Raptor to a FlexCard
questions.explanation: Filtering on an indexed field makes the query selective, and a row limit bounds the result set, which addresses both the slowness and the row-count risk. Removing the filter returns even more rows. Running the query in a loop multiplies the queries and hits limits. A FlexCard is a display component and does not fix the query.
